summary:
The Utah State Parks Adjustment Act, Pub. L. No. 118-181, requires specified federal land conveyances to the State of Utah for inclusion in three Utah State parks, without consideration and by quitclaim deed, subject to valid existing rights. The Act does not amend the United States Code and contains no authorization of appropriations or direct appropriation.

Section 1 designates the short title. Section 2(a) directs the Secretary of the Interior, not later than 180 days after enactment, to convey to Utah all right, title, and interest of the United States in specified Bureau of Land Management land identified for conveyance on the map titled “Antelope Island State Park Proposal: Utah State Park Additions,” dated February 28, 2023, for inclusion in Antelope Island State Park. The State must pay all conveyance-related costs, including surveys and administrative costs.

Section 2(b) similarly directs the Secretary of the Interior, within 180 days, to convey specified Bureau of Land Management land identified on the map titled “Wasatch Mountain State Park Proposal Utah State Park Additions,” dated May 3, 2024, for inclusion in Wasatch Mountain State Park, with all conveyance-related costs borne by the State.

Section 2(c) directs the Secretary of Agriculture, within 180 days, to convey specified National Forest System land identified on the map titled “S. 2136—Utah State Parks Adjustment Act,” dated September 12, 2023, together with any improvements, for inclusion in Fremont Indian State Park. As conditions of that conveyance, the Secretary must reserve easements for all National Forest System roads and trails that originate at, terminate at, or traverse the conveyed land, and may convey only the United States-held water rights identified in the Utah State Engineer database as 63-44, 63-1607, and 63-2817, which provide water to Castle Rock Campground and the Belknap Historic Guard Station interpretive site. If the Secretary determines a survey is necessary, the acreage and legal description must be established by a Secretary-approved survey, with reasonable survey costs paid by the State. The Secretary of Agriculture may enter into an agreement with Utah imposing additional terms concerning management and maintenance of the Belknap site, roads and trails, continued permitted livestock grazing, Forest Service access to retained water rights, and other post-conveyance management matters.

Section 2(d) authorizes minor map modifications, including survey-related changes. Section 2(e) requires conveyed land to be used for public purposes, including parks, campgrounds, recreation, and permitted livestock grazing, and provides a discretionary reversionary interest to the United States if such use ceases.
